Time-lagged common environmental disturbance (thermal, vibrational, or electromagnetic) with apparatus-specific equilibration delays; weak cross-correlations reflect weak driver magnitude or high noise floor
Calibration offset or scaling artifact in one apparatus chain (fixed gain error, transduction mismatch, or software bug); compounded by independent thermal or mechanical drifts in each chain

Undocumented apparatus-specific or environmental factor: calibration drift during baseline (days 1–10) not reset on day 11, apparatus crosstalk via shared power/mechanical coupling, or measurement geometry preferentially coupling to ~4-day environmental cycle

White noise with time-varying quantization or transducer gain; Day 38 variance spike is outlier or reflects instrument state change (e.g., resonator_obs power supply ripple, pendulum_obs optical misalignment); drift z-scores remain valid under heteroscedasticity but confidence bands widen.

Real small negative drift (0.002–0.005 unit/week) in baseline period (Days 1–10) reflecting apparatus equilibration or thermal stabilization; Day 38 variance spike masks ongoing stability; drift reversed or plateau by Day 35+ as systems reached equilibrium.

Measurement system instability or gain modulation on Day 38 specifically (power supply transient, optical coupling fluctuation, or software logging glitch); Day 38 variance is artifact, not signal; earlier baseline and post-baseline periods are reliably homoscedastic and drift signal is valid but small.

Weak shared environmental cyclic disturbance (3–6 day period in building HVAC, external weather, or seismic background) with apparatus-specific damping and lag; Day 38 variance spike reflects coherent environmental transient or resonance in one apparatus.
Calibration offset or scaling artifact in one apparatus chain compounded by independent noise; offset is static, drift is noise, Day 38 variance is independent transient.

Undocumented apparatus state change during baseline (Days 1–10) calibration drift not reset, optical alignment shift, or environmental transient during baseline establishment; Day 38 variance spike is unrelated.

Baseline apparatus equilibration: genuine small negative drift in Days 1–10 reflecting thermal stabilization, mechanical settling, or resonator frequency equilibration; post-baseline drift z-scores are valid signals of real early transient; Day 38 variance spike is orthogonal instrumental noise unrelated to drift mechanism.

White noise with time-varying measurement error floor: drift z-scores reflect heteroscedasticity rather than true signal; Days 1–10 baseline was low-noise period by chance or operator technique, post-baseline and Day 38 show true measurement noise regime; negative drift signs are random clustering within noise, not real phenomenon.

Measurement system artifact on Day 38 specifically: power supply transient, optical coupling fluctuation, software logging glitch, or environmental disturbance caused variance spike on Day 38 only; baseline and post-baseline periods (Days 1–37) are homoscedastic and drift signal is valid but small; Day 38 should be excluded as outlier from drift analysis.

Weak shared environmental cyclic disturbance with 3–6 day period: building HVAC, external weather, or seismic background drives low-amplitude oscillations in all apparatus with apparatus-specific damping and lag; cross-correlations at 3–6 day lags are signal, not noise; Day 38 variance spike reflects apparatus crossing resonance or achieving maximum excursion in oscillatory cycle.

Calibration offset or scaling artifact compounded by independent noise: lab and observational apparatus show ~1.5× scale factor (lab/obs ratios: pendulum 1.495, resonator 1.500), suggesting fixed gain error in observational chain; offset is static, drift z-scores reflect noise, Day 38 variance is transient unrelated to calibration.
